name: ai-panel-resize-drag-does-not-flicker
description:
Dragging the AI panel's left edge flickered: the drag read e.clientX, which is relative to the panel's own WebView, and that WebView's left edge moves on every width push, so each pointer move fed the next one a shifted origin. The panel edge zigzagged +14/-7 px through a one-way drag. The fix reads e.screenX at both ends, as sidebar-drag.js does.

A pointer-relative bug cannot be caught by a synthetic DOM event, so this drags the real grip with cgevent. A requestAnimationFrame sampler records window.innerWidth through the drag: the panel document IS the panel, so its innerWidth is the width the drag produced, frame by frame. A one-way widening drag must never narrow between two samples. The count of backward steps is the flicker, and it must be zero.

The capture is the recording a person can watch for blank or stale frames and for the web card staying with the panel edge.

actions.note: the panel's width and the grip's centre inside it. screenX is 0 in this WebView, so the grip's screen x is derived instead: the window is 1024 wide at x=0 (see ax_window_count), which puts the panel's left edge at 1024-280 and the grip at 744. An assertion pins both numbers, so a layout move fails loudly instead of dragging empty background

actions.expression: (() => { window.__aipw = [window.innerWidth]; const tick = () => { const w = window.innerWidth; if (w !== window.__aipw[window.__aipw.length - 1]) { window.__aipw.push(w); } window.__aipr = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }; tick(); return String(window.__aipw.length); })()
actions.note: records every width the panel actually reaches, in order, deduplicated so a still frame is not a sample
one way, leftwards, so the panel only ever widens - 140 points over 40 steps at cgevent's 20ms cadence

actions.expression: (() => { cancelAnimationFrame(window.__aipr); const w = window.__aipw; let back = 0; for (let i = 1; i < w.length; i++) { if (w[i] < w[i - 1]) { back++; } } return String(back); })()
(() => { const w = window.__aipw; return String(w[w.length - 1] - w[0]); })()

assertions.desc: setup: the hotkey opened the panel
setup: the grip sits where the drag below starts. A layout change moves it and this fails, rather than the drag quietly grabbing nothing

THE CONTROL: the drag really widened the panel, from DEFAULT_WIDTH 280 to the MAX_WIDTH_CAP 400 its 140 points of travel run into. Without this the backstep count below passes on a drag that never landed
a one-way widening drag never narrows between two frames. Before the fix the edge zigzagged +14/-7 px per move, which is what the recording showed as flicker
